summary: Swarm Defense builds small drones, and the software that lets one operator fly several of them, in Auburn Hills, Michigan. Products include the Kiwi, a quadcopter ordered in a one-way attack configuration, and target drones for counter-drone training. It says it grew out of Firefly Drone Shows, a light-show drone maker.
thesis: Swarm Defense announced a minimum $25 million Department of War order for 4,000 Kiwi attack drones. The only equity on record is $1,435,000. The company says its swarm control software was developed over eight years of drone light shows.
stage: A Form D filed 17 April 2026 reports $1,435,000 of equity sold to 10 investors (one non-accredited) and names none. FPDS shows $1,174,176 obligated across three awards. The company won no delivery order after Gauntlet I, placed fifth in Gauntlet II deep strike, and announced the minimum $25 million, 4,000-drone prototype order on 22 September 2026. It was not in FPDS on 2 October 2026.

team.name: Kyle Dorosz
team.background: CEO and founder (company release), the only executive officer and director named on the Form D. Founded Firefly with Ryan Sigmon in 2017 (New York Times).

team.name: Adam Wright
team.background: President, described in both company releases as a former Navy SEAL. No source read gives his start date or prior employers.

team.name: Ryan Sigmon
team.background: Founded Firefly with Dorosz and decided with him in 2024 to shift to defense drones (New York Times). No source read gives him a title at Swarm Defense.

team.name: Jonathan Hearl
team.background: Chief pilot officer, per a U.S. Army National Guard photo caption showing him operating Swarm Threat Emulator drones at Camp Grayling, Michigan, on 7 August 2026.

questions: What is the relationship with Firefly Drone Shows: which entity owns the swarm software, flight controller designs and employees, and do the two share a cap table?
Who are the 10 investors in the $1,435,000 on the Form D, on what terms, and is a larger raise planned to fund the 4,000-drone order?
On the Kiwi order, what is the delivery schedule, who supplies the munitions, and how much of the roughly $6,250 per drone stays with Swarm Defense?
What is actual monthly output today? The February 2026 release says capacity of 72,000 units a year, and a March 2026 WNEM report says 12,000 a year.
risks: Separation from Firefly Drone Shows is unclear. The company says it spun out in August 2024 and shares resources with Firefly. The New York Times describes a rename.
The program behind its one large order re-ranks vendors each round. It won no delivery order after Gauntlet I and placed fifth of five in Gauntlet II deep strike.
Delivering an armed product at this scale is unproven. The New York Times described October 2025 output as target drones under 2 pounds. The company gave no delivery schedule.
unverified: The company claims capacity of 72,000 units a year, a single operator controlling 2,000+ drones and a fully NDAA-compliant supply chain. None is independently confirmed.
A PitchBook search snippet lists a $1.44M seed round on 17 April 2026, not confirmed. The Form D does not call the round a seed.
A search snippet says Adam Wright served a decade as a Navy SEAL and a LinkedIn snippet gives University of Chicago Booth. Neither page could be opened.

announcement.what: A State of Michigan press release named Swarm Defense among the 2025 Mobility Prototyping Grant winners, for a target drone production line.
